name: orc_extraction_r134a
title: ORC with two-stage expander and intermediate extraction (R134a)
summary: R134a Organic Rankine Cycle (T_ev = 90 °C, T_cd = 30 °C) whose screw/scroll-type expander is described stage by stage: isentropic first expansion, extraction of 13 % of the flow at an intermediate pressure, isentropic second expansion and constant-volume discharge; the extracted vapour is mixed with the exhaust and cools the pumped liquid in an internal heat exchanger. Determines the pressures, all state points, a 4.99 kW expander power, 35.6 kW boiler duty and a cycle efficiency of 11.7 %.

authors: S. Quoilin (ULiège Thermodynamics Laboratory) — probable, to be confirmed by the maintainer
origin.ees_version: X9.920 (CoolSolve EES_ok/orc_extraction.EES); identical equations in X7.991 (thermo_models/modeles/cycle a extraction.EES, TM-0267)
origin.language: en (3 French comments in the diagram section)

verification.reference: Solution stored in the original EES file (CoolSolve misc/EES_ok.zip, EES_ok/orc_extraction.EES, EES 9.920, 132 stored variables); the equations of that file are byte-identical to ~/Nextcloud/thermo_models/modeles/cycle a extraction.EES (EES 7.991)
verification.notes: 132 common variables: 52 agree within 0.1 %. The 52 h/u/s variables differ by a constant reference-state offset (+148.19 kJ/kg, +795.79 J/(kg K): EES default R134a reference vs CoolProp IIR); after removing it they agree within 0.09 %. Remaining deviations 0.1-0.2 % (R134a equation of state): specific volumes +0.21 %, mass flow -0.21 %, Q_dot_ev -0.16 %, Q_dot_cd -0.17 %, W_dot_exp -0.12 %, W_dot_pp -0.20 %, eta +0.06 %. EES quality() outside the dome: -100/100 sentinels vs 0 in CoolSolve (diagnostic only). The original is over-determined (5 variables defined twice or three times, 2 never defined): the free inputs were restored with the stored values and the redundant definitions removed without changing any equation of the physics.
